cells.tense: Here, with the pen, you are weighing what has weight and it is holding steady.
cells.ask: Take something that has run its course and answer, by your own hand, whether it is still yours to keep or finished. Keep it or release it, and don't announce the answer to anyone.
cells.core:
At a door like this, where something is ending, you can weigh what has weight without ducking the scale. You feel the pull of the thing and still give it a clean ending, and the ending lands fair. A door out is a door in, and you are not standing in the frame. What is done stops asking you for a verdict.

That weighing is not a mood; it is a small piece you can do. Take something that has run its course and answer, by your own hand, whether it is still yours to keep or finished. The deciding is yours, and telling no one keeps it honest. The reading does not have to be right about your week for the weighing to still count.
cells.sheetLine: You can end a thing cleanly, and the ending lands fair.
cells.verb: Weighing what has weight, and giving the finished thing a clean end
cells.place: At the door where what was must finish before what comes next can begin

cells.tense: In the future you are already at the next door, braced, before this one has finished closing.
cells.act: hold the weight as a builder holds stone
cells.ask: Name an ending you have been trying to get finished this week, then hold it the way a builder holds stone — steady, no pushing, no deadline. Let a day pass with no move on it.
cells.core:
Where you are headed, no ending gets to be an ending. You are already at the next door in your mind, bracing, and the endings here get weighed before they have finished happening. It is easy to keep handling a thing past the point where it was done, managing what was already released, calling that fairness. Wait, with no hand on the scale yet. The heaviest part of finishing may be the part where you do not touch it.

Try holding one ending the way a builder holds stone: steady, no pushing. Name the ending you have been trying to get finished this week, and let a day pass without a move on it. If it still carries its own weight, that tells you something worth knowing.

cells.tense: In the past, you are still at a door that is already behind you, and no finishing has come.
cells.act: write the facts down in order, without feeling words
cells.ask: Set down what happened, in the sequence it happened, and keep every feeling word off the page. Once it's all there, read it twice through — then close the notebook.
cells.core:
At a door like this that has gone behind you, the finishing did not come. You keep handling a thing that already ended, and the scale sits untouched. The ability is there; you can weigh. What is gone is the tidy moment where an ending gets settled, and going back for one only adds weight to the load.

Thinking harder will not settle it. One piece of practice will: set down what happened, in the sequence it happened, and keep every feeling word off the page. Not the story, not what you wish had happened — the plain sequence. Read it twice through, then close the notebook. That discipline works without a good mood behind it. What you are after is not a verdict; it is the plain order of what happened, so the door stops opening on you at night.

cells.core:
Endings keep going well around you — things get let go, rooms get cleared — and your account has you just getting through it. You are the one who gives the thing its clean out; the door did not open by itself. You can hear where a person actually stands, and you use it quietly, with nothing announced.

Go back to the simple form of it. Ask someone who lived through an ending you handled what it was like from where they stood — one question, no defending your side of it. Listen for the part you do not already know, which will be the part worth keeping. Curiosity came before judgment for you, once. The answer needs nothing done with it, and the asking is enough as it stands.

attempts.check: The claim my Balance core makes — that some specific ending has recently been carried out fairly and cleanly — is not in the record, so I keep the balance seated in one recognisable moment rather than in a history. Objection: a reader could say they are not cleaning anything up right now, only feeling their way through a door someone else closed. The ask survives that: weighing what has weight, in your own hands, after the door is behind you, does not need the ending to have been chosen or even finished. The sentence serving the writer's cleverness more than the person: 'when something is over, you know exactly when to let go'; it is out — that is a person's own report, not mine to issue. Same for 'fair emotional judgment' on glass, which is the record's phrase, not kitchen-table language.
